title: Spectral bounds and their limits in Pauli contextuality: exact configurations and a proof of Jonah's Conjecture E
peer_review_status: Research preprint (not peer reviewed; AI-assisted under human direction; listed on ORCID)
author: Alexander Stephen Donahue
core_result: Unified study with complete Lean 4.35.0 formalizations (100 newly audited declarations across 12 modules, 13,910 library lines, plus retained audits) of the spectral floor and its asymptotic 1/2 Filter.Tendsto limits (Theorem 1, Corollary A), Theorem 2 (Kramers / quaternionic floor and elliptic quadrics Q-(2N-1,2)), Theorems 3-4 (5-way saturation equivalences and (2^N-1)|S| = square), Propositions 3, 8, 10, exact degrees 75 (4 qubits), 480 (5 qubits), 2016 (6 qubits) and 729344 (7 qubits), Theorem 13b (infinite non-closed contextual floor-saturating pure-CCZ determinant family |Psi_{3m}> for every m >= 1 proved directly from the state vector, plus a 540.3M-form N=9 cyclic-symmetry rank-8 C census), symplectic transvection invariance, CSS witnesses (315, 1575, 6975), exact double-counting ladders, unconditional bounds d(W(7,2)) >= 1455 and d(Q+(9,2)) >= 6444, Lemmas L1/L4 and master reduction paired with an independent 42-orbit W(5,2) C census and pure-integer dual check reproducing Jonah [J1]'s (315, 1575, 6975), a four-qubit cospectral C3 pair with distinct completion spectra (Theorem 14) and EXACT global binary completion optima min_y F(sigma_0, y) = 368 and min_y F(sigma_1, y) = 344 with exact gap 24 (Theorem 16'' via kernel-checked pure-integer MET-SDP duals), general cone lift and case C11 from C3 (Corollary 18), signed-Clifford orbit transport, Lemmas 20-21, Theorem 22 (universal cubic-trace identity) and Table 8 outside character sums, and Theorem 19: a full machine-checked Lean 4 proof of Jonah's Conjecture E at the canonical Hermitian eigenvalue-multiset level across all nine vertex cases (C1, C3, C5, C6, C8, C11, C12, C14, C15) for every N >= 4 (plus N >= 3 for C1, C3, C6, C11), accompanied by 202/202 exact verifier checks on Ubuntu 24.04 CI.
verification_boundary: As of v1.8.0, the spectral floor and asymptotic 1/2 limits, Kramers quaternionic floor, 5-way saturation equivalences, Propositions 3/8/10, saturated configurations (75, 480, 2016, 729344), Theorem 13b infinite pure-CCZ determinant family |Psi_{3m}> for all m >= 1 directly from the state vector, symplectic transvection invariance, CSS witnesses (315, 1575, 6975), exact double-counting ladders, unconditional Kramers-lifted bounds d(W(7,2)) >= 1455 and d(Q+(9,2)) >= 6444, Lemmas L1/L4 and master reduction, four-qubit C3 spectral certificate (42 decls) and EXACT global binary completion optima min F(sigma_0) = 368 and min F(sigma_1) = 344 with exact gap 24 (Theorem 16'' via pure-integer MET-SDP duals, plus Corollary 16 & Proposition 16'), all-qubit C3 family (74 decls), general cone lift and case C11 (Corollary 18), signed-Clifford orbit transport, Lemmas 20-21, Theorem 22, and eigenvalue-multiset Theorem 19 (Jonah's Conjecture E in all 9 vertex cases for every N >= 4) are all kernel-checked in Lean 4.35.0 (100 audited declarations in VerifyNewFormalizations.lean, 13,910 library lines across 12 modules, zero sorry, zero native_decide, strictly standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]). Remaining outside Lean: state-to-mask identifications of finite Table 1 rows other than |Psi_{3m}>, Propositions 4, 6, 9 and 11, exhaustive enumerations of Theorems 12-13, the 540.3M-form N=9 rank-8 cyclic census, the independent 42-orbit W(5,2) C census and 42 pure-integer certificates reproducing Jonah [J1], printed C3 factorizations and spherical relaxation gap 32, and the single-orbit group-transitivity classification of Jonah [J3, Theorem B4]. Historical source manuscripts remain preserved inside the repository as component records of this single combined study (see publication/PAPER-MAP.md). Superseded GitHub repository archived read-only on 2026-11-24 and consolidated into 0TH-2026-009 (0thernes/pauli-contextuality-lab); this historical snapshot remains cryptographically pinned.
